headline: Broad Rally Takes Hold as Materials and Healthcare Lead Friday's Session
body_html:
Equities are posting a decidedly constructive mid-session tone on Friday, with advancers outnumbering decliners roughly 378 to 167 across the tracked universe of 550 names. Materials are setting the pace with a gain of 1.32%, followed closely by Healthcare at 1.20% and Homebuilders at 1.04%, suggesting defensive and commodity-linked positioning is resonating with traders as geopolitical anxieties surrounding Iran and the Strait of Hormuz persist into the weekend.

The standout mover of the session is TG Therapeutics, surging 9.26% to top the leaderboard, with Albemarle close behind at 7.15% — a lithium name benefiting from renewed materials enthusiasm and a firmer gold backdrop that has drawn fresh capital into commodity-adjacent equities. Tesla is also attracting notable buying interest, adding 5.39% midday, while Estee Lauder and Ross Stores round out a consumer-flavored secondary tier of gainers.

The sole sector in the red is Semiconductors, off 0.62%, as Marvell Technology slides 6.31% and testing-equipment specialist Teradyne drops 3.25%. Networking hardware name Ubiquiti is also under pressure, falling 5.16%. Into the close, watch whether the chip-sector drag widens or stabilizes — that dynamic will shape the day's final complexion.

briefs.headline: Albemarle Surges as Gold Rebound Lifts Materials Complex
briefs.body: Albemarle is advancing 7.15% at midday, contributing to the Materials sector's 1.32% lead over the broader tape. A rebound in gold prices — driven by bond-market anxiety, dollar softness, and elevated debt concerns — is drawing renewed interest into commodity and materials names broadly.

briefs.headline: Citadel Confirms Major Drawdown of Situational Awareness Risk Book
briefs.body: Ken Griffin's Citadel has disclosed that it unwound more than 80% of risk tied to a specific situational-awareness-oriented portfolio, a significant de-risking move that is drawing attention across the hedge-fund community. The disclosure adds to a broader conversation about positioning as geopolitical tensions weigh on market sentiment heading into the weekend.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Traffic Drops to Single Digits, Tightening Oil Supply Calculus
briefs.body: Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen to single-digit vessel counts according to tracking data, intensifying supply-route concerns in an already strained energy market. Brent crude is on pace for a second consecutive weekly gain as U.S. pressure on Iranian exports mounts and Tehran vows a forceful response to further economic restrictions.

briefs.headline: Marvell Leads Semiconductor Selloff as Sector Bucks Broad Rally
briefs.body: Marvell Technology is the session's largest decliner, shedding 6.31% and pulling the Semiconductors sector down 0.62% — the only group in negative territory at midday. Fabrinet and Teradyne are also lower by 3.68% and 3.25%, respectively, suggesting targeted pressure on technology-hardware and chip-adjacent names rather than a wholesale risk-off move.

briefs.headline: TG Therapeutics Jumps Over 9% to Claim Session's Top Spot
briefs.body: Biotech name TG Therapeutics is the day's clear standout, rising 9.26% to lead all gainers in the tracked universe. The move lifts the Healthcare sector to a 1.20% gain, with telehealth name Hims & Hers Health adding further support at 5.74%, reflecting broad appetite for healthcare exposure on the final trading day of the week.

briefs.headline: European Equities Climb on Commodity Tailwinds Despite Weekly Losses
briefs.body: European shares are advancing Friday, buoyed by rising gold prices and resilient commodity-linked names, though major indices remain on track to post a net weekly decline. Analysts note that war-affected European markets have demonstrated more durability than broadly feared, even as the six-month conflict anniversary draws fresh scrutiny from global investors.
